Position Summary...

What You'll Do...Position Summary

We are seeking a strategic and execution-focused Director of Software Engineering to lead the transformation of Walmart’s Tax-Exempt technology ecosystem into a unified omni-channel platform serving both brick-and-mortar and eCommerce experiences across Walmart and Sam’s Club. This leader will drive the modernization, consolidation, and scalability of tax-exempt capabilities while ensuring compliance, operational excellence, and exceptional customer experiences.

This role is responsible for building and leading a high-performing U.S.-based engineering organization focused on delivering resilient, scalable, and compliant solutions that simplify tax exempt purchasing for customers across all channels. The Director will partner closely with Product, Architecture, Tax, Compliance, Legal, Operations, and business stakeholders to accelerate the technology roadmap while reducing compliance risk and enabling long-term platform growth.

The ideal candidate combines deep engineering leadership with strong architectural vision, operational rigor, stakeholder management, and the ability to translate evolving tax laws and regulatory requirements into scalable technical solutions.

What You’ll Do

Lead Omni-Channel Tax Exempt Transformation

Define and execute the engineering strategy for a unified Tax-Exempt platform spanning:
Walmart stores
Walmart eCommerce
Sam’s Club stores
Sam’s Club digital experiences

Drive consolidation of fragmented systems and workflows into a scalable enterprise platform with shared services and consistent customer experiences.
Enable seamless omni-channel tax exempt journeys including registration, validation, purchasing, renewals, audits, and customer support.

Drive Engineering Excellence

Establish and scale engineering best practices across architecture, development, testing, security, observability, and operational reliability.
Build a culture centered on engineering quality, accountability, automation, and continuous improvement.
Improve platform resiliency, scalability, performance, and maintainability while reducing operational and compliance risk.
Champion modern software engineering practices including CI/CD, cloud-native architecture, automated testing, infrastructure as code, and developer productivity tooling.

Architect for Scale and Compliance

Lead architectural direction for enterprise-grade tax exempt systems handling high transaction volumes and complex compliance requirements.
Ensure solutions are designed with strong governance, auditability, traceability, and data integrity controls.
Partner with enterprise architecture teams to define standards, reusable patterns, APIs, and integration strategies across Walmart and Sam’s ecosystems.
Balance speed of delivery with long-term sustainability and regulatory compliance.

Accelerate Business Roadmap Delivery

Partner with Product and business stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into executable engineering roadmaps.
Drive predictable delivery across multiple concurrent initiatives while managing technical debt and platform modernization.
Create execution transparency through measurable outcomes, operational metrics, and delivery governance.
Identify opportunities to simplify customer experiences and unlock new business capabilities through technology innovation.

Partner Across Business and Compliance Functions

Build strong partnerships with Tax, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Product, Operations, and Store organizations.
Develop a deep understanding of federal, state, and local tax-exempt regulations and ensure engineering solutions align with evolving legal requirements.
Act as a trusted technical advisor to executive stakeholders on compliance risk, platform strategy, and investment priorities.
Lead cross-functional communication during audits, regulatory reviews, and major business initiatives.

Build and Develop a High-Caliber Engineering Organization

Recruit, retain, and develop exceptional U.S.-based engineering talent with a strong focus on technical excellence and ownership.
Create a culture of mentorship, inclusion, innovation, and high performance.
Develop organizational capabilities in distributed systems, compliance engineering, platform engineering, and enterprise architecture.
Establish clear career growth paths, succession planning, and leadership development across the organization.

Imagine working in an environment where one line of code can make life easier for hundreds of millions of people. That’s what we do at Walmart Global Tech. We’re a team of software engineers, data scientists, cybersecurity expert's and service professionals within the world’s leading retailer who make an epic impact and are at the forefront of the next retail disruption. People are why we innovate, and people power our innovations. We are people-led and tech-empowered. We train our team in the skillsets of the future and bring in experts like you to help us grow. We have roles for those chasing their first opportunity as well as those looking for the opportunity that will define their career. Here, you can kickstart a great career in tech, gain new skills and experience for virtually every industry, or leverage your expertise to innovate at scale, impact millions and reimagine the future of retail.

Walmart’s culture is a competitive advantage, and it’s fostered by being together. Working together in person allows us to collaborate, align quickly and innovate with greater speed. We use our campuses to create purposeful connection rooted in deepening understanding and investing in the development of our associates.

Now Assist, Virtual Agent, agentic AI, and AI-enabled service experiences

Ensure solutions remain scalable, secure, upgradeable, supportable, and aligned with enterprise architecture principles.

Overview

We are looking for an Optical Validation Engineering, Senior Director to drive the characterization, validation, and qualification of near-packaged optics (NPO) and co-packaged optics (CPO) systems. In this role, you will define and implement the validation approach that ensures the optical, electrical, and thermal performance of advanced photonic interconnects used in next-generation data center and networking platforms.

You will work at the intersection of silicon photonics, packaging, electrical design, and systems engineering to ensure robust product performance from prototype to production.

Key Responsibilities

Lead a team that owns the optical validation strategy and roadmap for optical connectivity products.
Develop and execute comprehensive validation and test plans covering optical coupling, insertion loss, signal integrity, thermal stability, and reliability metrics.
Define optical test methodologies for complex integrated systems involving photonic, electrical, and mechanical interfaces.
Collaborate with design, packaging, and system architecture teams to translate product specifications into measurable validation criteria.
Establish automated test frameworks for high-throughput optical and electrical validation (instrument control, data analysis, and reporting).
Analyze measurement data to identify performance trends, failure modes, and root causes.
Lead design-of-experiments (DOE) initiatives to optimize system performance and yield.
Interface with manufacturing, reliability, and quality teams to ensure seamless transition to volume production and long-term reliability.
Mentor junior engineers and promote best practices in optical validation and measurement science.

Qualifications

M.S. or Ph.D. in Optical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or equivalent field.
8+ years of experience in optical module testing, photonic component validation, or high-speed interconnect qualification.
Deep understanding of optical measurements (IL, RL, BER, eye diagrams, mode coupling), optical alignment, and signal characterization.
Hands-on experience with optical instrumentation (optical spectrum analyzers, BERTs, network analyzers, power meters, interferometers).
Strong background in data analysis, automation scripting (Python, LabVIEW, MATLAB), and statistical validation methods.
Familiarity with packaging-related optical performance dependencies (thermo-mechanical stress, optical coupling efficiency, etc.).
Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with a proven ability to align across multidisciplinary hardware teams.

Preferred Experience

Experience with co-packaged optics, silicon photonics assemblies, and near-packaged optical interfaces.
Knowledge of industry standards and compliance testing (IEEE 802.3, OIF, or custom CPO protocols).
Understanding of reliability qualification (HTOL, TC, mechanical shock/vibration for optical components).
Familiarity with system-level validation for networking and hyperscale data center environments.

You will sit in real ambiguity: what we want to build, what we are already funded to build, how to prioritize across both, and how product strategy can help create new funding opportunities. You will help translate that ambiguity into decisions—a portfolio roadmap, build/no-build calls, and sequenced priorities. Reporting to Sage’s CTO, you will be accountable for outcomes, not just plans: the success of the products that serve our research programs, the balance between strategy and delivery, and the adoption and impact of what we build, both inside Sage and across the broader research community.

AI is rapidly reshaping how researchers work with data. The ecosystem already includes AI-powered tools and AI research partnerships, and a central part of this role is applying strong product judgment to identify where AI creates genuine value for researchers—and where it does not. Working closely with technical and research leaders, this role will help Sage build and evolve AI-enabled capabilities responsibly.

Most of our product portfolio is grant-funded and serves our research programs. A smaller, emerging part of the picture is helping the ecosystem grow more sustainably, including a modest and growing set of commercial offerings. That commercial dimension is a tiny slice today; we are looking for someone who can help shape and grow it carefully and thoughtfully, without losing sight of the much larger community of researchers the ecosystem exists to serve. Like the rest of our team, you will work in an AI-forward environment and prioritize productivity and impact over arbitrary processes.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the product portfolio and its outcomes. In close partnership with the CTO, ensure the product portfolio meets the needs of our programs and users—not just that it is coordinated. Bring clarity to competing priorities, make tradeoffs visible, and drive the cross-portfolio prioritization, build/no-build, and sequencing decisions that no single domain owner can make alone. Ensure capabilities that serve multiple teams are thoughtfully aligned and built once, rather than duplicated across the ecosystem.
Balance strategy with delivery. Partner with the CTO and engineering leadership to evolve the long-term product vision while maintaining focus on near-term execution. Translate strategy into actionable priorities and remain accountable not only for the roadmap, but for what gets built, delivered, and adopted.
Drive adoption and impact, internally and externally. Measure success by whether products are genuinely used and create value: internally by Sage’s programs and teams, and externally by researchers, institutions, and partners. Establish a strong understanding of adoption and impact, and close the gap between what we build and what our users need.
Stay close to users and funders. Build trusted relationships with researchers, principal investigators, program officers, and institutional partners. Maintain a direct listening cadence, bring user insights into product decisions, and partner with program teams to ensure the ecosystem continues to evolve around real research needs.
Shape where AI fits in the product. Partner with the CTO, engineering teams, and research leaders to identify where AI-powered capabilities and partnerships create genuine value for researchers—and where they do not. Apply strong product judgment to help Sage build and deliver AI-enabled products responsibly, thoughtfully, and in alignment with our mission.
Grow the ecosystem’s commercial offerings thoughtfully. Partner with leadership to shape a modest and growing set of commercial offerings, including their positioning, pricing, and user experience, helping the ecosystem become more sustainable while remaining grounded in Sage’s mission and research community.
Connect product strategy to funding opportunities. Work closely with principal investigators, program leaders, and executive leadership to make product investments clear, compelling, and fundable. Identify opportunities where product strategy can support new research initiatives and partnerships, and help shape product concepts into proposals that can be carried forward.
Lead and grow the Product Team. Provide direction and support for product managers and portfolio owners who define, validate, and steward products across the ecosystem. Partner with the CTO to continue evolving the product function, develop talent, establish effective product practices, and grow the team along the product career ladder.
Champion product design and user experience. Partner with design leadership to establish product design principles, standards, and practices across the ecosystem. Ensure Sage’s products provide a coherent, intuitive experience for researchers and partners, with hands-on craft supported by senior design expertise.
Partner with executive leadership on product direction. Serve as a strategic thought partner to the CTO and senior leadership team, helping translate organizational goals, research priorities, and technical opportunities into a cohesive product strategy. Collaborate across Sage to make thoughtful decisions about where to invest, where to experiment, and where to say no.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Deepgram's ambition is to build a generational company with a small, exceptional team — which only works if every engineer and every function operates with serious AI leverage. We're looking for a Head of AI Enablement Engineering

Want to define how an entire company works with AI — and you'd rather build the proof than write the memo.

new_jobs.title: Head of Product, Technology
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Sage Bionetworks uses open science and collaboration to improve human health. We turn complex biomedical data into actionable insights through responsible sharing, strong governance, and innovative tools like AI. Our team values curiosity, diverse perspectives, and experimentation.

The Opportunity

Sage Bionetworks is looking for a Head of Product for Synapse.org and its ecosystem of biomedical tools, knowledge portals, and services. The ecosystem serves tens of thousands of individual scientists and the institutions and programs they work within. Serving this broad community well is at the heart of this role. The Head of Product will spend significant time in the field—with individual scientists, PIs, program officers, and institutional partners—and bring that ground truth back into every roadmap and portfolio decision.

This is a new, integrating role. Our product domains have owners and our engineering operation has leads, but no one today is responsible for making the portfolio add up across programs while holding the end-to-end experience of the people who actually use the ecosystem. The Head of Product will be that connector: partnering closely with the CTO, product owners, engineering leaders, and program teams to create clarity across the portfolio.

You will sit in real ambiguity: what we want to build, what we are already funded to build, how to prioritize across both, and how product strategy can help create new funding opportunities. You will help translate that ambiguity into decisions—a portfolio roadmap, build/no-build calls, and sequenced priorities. Reporting to Sage’s CTO, you will be accountable for outcomes, not just plans: the success of the products that serve our research programs, the balance between strategy and delivery, and the adoption and impact of what we build, both inside Sage and across the broader research community.

AI is rapidly reshaping how researchers work with data. The ecosystem already includes AI-powered tools and AI research partnerships, and a central part of this role is applying strong product judgment to identify where AI creates genuine value for researchers—and where it does not. Working closely with technical and research leaders, this role will help Sage build and evolve AI-enabled capabilities responsibly.

Most of our product portfolio is grant-funded and serves our research programs. A smaller, emerging part of the picture is helping the ecosystem grow more sustainably, including a modest and growing set of commercial offerings. That commercial dimension is a tiny slice today; we are looking for someone who can help shape and grow it carefully and thoughtfully, without losing sight of the much larger community of researchers the ecosystem exists to serve. Like the rest of our team, you will work in an AI-forward environment and prioritize productivity and impact over arbitrary processes.

Note:
Please do not upload your resume as your cover letter (required)

Key Responsibilities

Lead the product portfolio and its outcomes. In close partnership with the CTO, ensure the product portfolio meets the needs of our programs and users—not just that it is coordinated. Bring clarity to competing priorities, make tradeoffs visible, and drive the cross-portfolio prioritization, build/no-build, and sequencing decisions that no single domain owner can make alone. Ensure capabilities that serve multiple teams are thoughtfully aligned and built once, rather than duplicated across the ecosystem.
Balance strategy with delivery. Partner with the CTO and engineering leadership to evolve the long-term product vision while maintaining focus on near-term execution. Translate strategy into actionable priorities and remain accountable not only for the roadmap, but for what gets built, delivered, and adopted.
Drive adoption and impact, internally and externally. Measure success by whether products are genuinely used and create value: internally by Sage’s programs and teams, and externally by researchers, institutions, and partners. Establish a strong understanding of adoption and impact, and close the gap between what we build and what our users need.
Stay close to users and funders. Build trusted relationships with researchers, principal investigators, program officers, and institutional partners. Maintain a direct listening cadence, bring user insights into product decisions, and partner with program teams to ensure the ecosystem continues to evolve around real research needs.
Shape where AI fits in the product. Partner with the CTO, engineering teams, and research leaders to identify where AI-powered capabilities and partnerships create genuine value for researchers—and where they do not. Apply strong product judgment to help Sage build and deliver AI-enabled products responsibly, thoughtfully, and in alignment with our mission.
Grow the ecosystem’s commercial offerings thoughtfully. Partner with leadership to shape a modest and growing set of commercial offerings, including their positioning, pricing, and user experience, helping the ecosystem become more sustainable while remaining grounded in Sage’s mission and research community.
Connect product strategy to funding opportunities. Work closely with principal investigators, program leaders, and executive leadership to make product investments clear, compelling, and fundable. Identify opportunities where product strategy can support new research initiatives and partnerships, and help shape product concepts into proposals that can be carried forward.
Lead and grow the Product Team. Provide direction and support for product managers and portfolio owners who define, validate, and steward products across the ecosystem. Partner with the CTO to continue evolving the product function, develop talent, establish effective product practices, and grow the team along the product career ladder.
Champion product design and user experience. Partner with design leadership to establish product design principles, standards, and practices across the ecosystem. Ensure Sage’s products provide a coherent, intuitive experience for researchers and partners, with hands-on craft supported by senior design expertise.
Partner with executive leadership on product direction. Serve as a strategic thought partner to the CTO and senior leadership team, helping translate organizational goals, research priorities, and technical opportunities into a cohesive product strategy. Collaborate across Sage to make thoughtful decisions about where to invest, where to experiment, and where to say no.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Life Sciences, Business, Human-Computer Interaction, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Advanced degree in a relevant technical, scientific, or business discipline is a plus.

Experience

10+ years of progressive experience in product management and product leadership, including responsibility for defining strategy and delivering outcomes across multiple products or an enterprise product portfolio.
Demonstrated success defining product vision and portfolio strategy, setting organizational priorities, and translating user needs into measurable product outcomes.
Experience building and leading high-performing product teams, developing product leaders, and establishing scalable product practices that enable teams to move quickly and make sound decisions.
Strong user-centered product judgment. You know how to listen to a broad community of users—from individual researchers to institutional stakeholders—and turn what you hear into clear product decisions.
A track record of influencing executive leaders and aligning engineering, design, science, and business stakeholders around difficult prioritization decisions and strategic tradeoffs.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity and turning competing priorities, incomplete information, and funding constraints into clear direction, sequencing, and execution.
Experience leading product strategy in a rapidly evolving AI landscape, with sound judgment about where AI creates genuine value for users—and where it doesn't.
Experience bringing AI-powered products, platforms, or strategic partnerships to market, with an appreciation for responsible AI development and governance.
Demonstrated accountability for product outcomes—not just roadmaps—including adoption, customer value, and organizational impact.
Excellent communication skills with the executive presence and credibility to influence senior leaders, represent product strategy with funders and external partners, and confidently make difficult prioritization decisions.

Nice to Have

Experience growing or scaling commercial products, including pricing, packaging, monetization, or taking products from free to paid while maintaining a strong user experience.
Experience balancing mission-driven impact with business sustainability in a nonprofit, research, academic, or grant-funded organization.
Experience in scientific research, biomedical data, healthcare, life sciences, or other data-intensive technical domains.
Familiarity with open science, research data platforms, data-sharing ecosystems, or open-source software communities.
Experience partnering with principal investigators, research institutions, government agencies, or funding organizations to shape product investments and support new funding opportunities.
Experience establishing product operating models, portfolio governance, and organizational product strategy across multiple teams.
Product design leadership experience, with a strong appreciation for usability, accessibility, and creating cohesive experiences across an interconnected product ecosystem.

Job Functions And Physical Requirements

The following cognitive and physical activities outline the essential functions required for successful job performance. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to fulfill these functions.

Physical Demands

Extended periods of sitting at a desk and using a computer.
Repeated wrist, hand, and finger movements.
Requires clear vision for tasks like data analysis, transcribing, computer use, and reading.
Occasionally lifting or moving objects weighing up to 10 pounds.

Cognitive Demands

Able to work effectively under deadlines.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Attention to detail and accuracy.
Flexibility to adapt to changing environments, priorities and multitask.

Additional Functions

Travel two times per year for on-site events in Seattle, WA.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Works well in a team and maintains professionalism.
Follows company policies, procedures, and relevant laws and regulations.

Note: This list is not exhaustive and may be subject to modification as job duties evolve.

Compensation & Total Rewards

Sage Bionetworks implements equitable workplace strategies to ensure fair pay. Actual compensation is determined by market data, specific experience, and internal parity.

Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, and long-term disability.
Future Security: Robust retirement plan and flexible spending accounts (FSA).
Work-Life Harmony: Paid time off and flexible work arrangements.
